- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to historical mean.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent peak or adjust downward if sentiment drops.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and price is rising, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to account for sentiment-driven momentum.
- Model frequently underestimates true price in early horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) when sentiment is neutral or negative; apply slight upward bias (0.5–1.0%) for short-term forecasts.
- For 10+ day forecasts, model shows persistent lag; add 0.8–1.2% to forecast to account for mean reversion toward historical 30-day average.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating high/low), model overfits to recent noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values before applying sentiment-weighted adjustment.
